quotes.text: Capture a PaymentIntent multiple times, up to the authorized amount.

old_evidence.text: Capture a PaymentIntent multiple times, up to the authorized amount.
Uncaptured PaymentIntents transition to `canceled`, while partially captured PaymentIntents transition to `succeeded`.
If you want to release the uncaptured funds for a partially captured payment, set the amount to 0 and set `final_capture` to `true`.

findings: Raw-content axis: navigation-only. November repeats the central behavior of multiple captures on a PaymentIntent up to its authorized amount and links three web variants (new raw lines 5-15, old raw lines 4-12, 319-323, 752-756). Neither the reduced length nor the query labels establish removal, fresh verification of operational details, or a different integration API.

May's three full variants give the operational gates: IC+ feature with contact-support path for blended pricing, online eligible card, manual capture, up to 50 captures per Intent, CUP and JCB country limits, no separate charges/transfers using source_transaction, and network/merchant constraints. Old raw lines 14-51, 325-362 and 758-792. Under automatic/automatic_async the request may be accepted and the Charge status may appear available even though the Intent automatically captures in full. The old note leaves later validation version behavior open (old raw lines 33-35, 344-346, 776-778).

May's hosted and embedded paths configure payment-mode Checkout Sessions for their resulting PaymentIntent, whereas Advanced directly creates and confirms a manual PaymentIntent. Hosted redirects via session.url and success_url; embedded uses ui_mode=embedded_page, session client secret/mount and return_url. Server-side capture operates on the PaymentIntent ID, with availability on latest_charge; authorized, capturable and received amounts are distinct. Old raw lines 53-125, 364-522, 794-865. The November ui=elements link is a guide URL selector only.

May's later sections distinguish non-final captures within authorization, finalization and release, possible partial refunds within captured less refunded amount, Connect parameters and per-capture/final webhook semantics (old raw lines 137-317, 570-750, 853-1033). Successful authorization, Checkout return/completion, feature status, capture and settlement/funds availability are distinct.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain 2026-05-11 provenance and the historical full variant details, including manual online card prerequisites; IC+ offering and blended contact guidance; region and 50-capture limits; feature request/availability and authorization/capture boundaries; testing, Connect, refunds and events (old raw lines 2-51, 137-317, 319-415, 752-1033). Keep November 7 provenance for purpose and navigation alone (new raw lines 2-15).

Keep the migration guide separately qualified to the May beta-to-GA use case. Its preconfirmation option, sample Stripe-Version header, full remaining amount with final_capture=false HTTP 400, non-final event change, and GA release of uncaptured funds without creating a refund are supported by raw/stripe-flexible-features-migration-2026.md:312-489. They are distinct from settings in the dedicated guide and cannot be upgraded to unconditional current claims by either index.

Keep the reported `charge.updated` and `payment_intent.amount_capturable_updated` per capture, `charge.captured` at final capture or authorization reversal on expiry, `captured` only after finalization/reversal, and `charge.refunded` after final capture plus full refund of the received amount. Retain the Connect-specific partial-refund flag and separate-charge route restrictions with their conditions (old raw lines 234-317, 950-1033).
conflicts: Existing baseline source lines 31-35 flatten expiration into final capture and omit the canceled versus succeeded distinction. Old raw lines 170-222, 603-655 and 886-938 distinguish zero prior capture (`canceled` on expiry) from partial capture (`succeeded` when finalized), and scope the explicit zero-amount final-release operation to an already partially captured payment. Expiry releases remaining authorization rather than creating a charge for the outstanding amount (old raw lines 293-308, 726-742, 1009-1025). Carry the same warning in wiki/concepts/stripe-multicapture.md:25-45.

Historical embedded Node example omits `payment_intent_data.capture_method=manual` (old raw lines 364-415), even though embedded availability at old raw lines 329-346 requires it. The hosted and direct examples explicitly set manual (old raw lines 109-117, 794-825). Preserve the manual requirement in source lines 18 and 27, expose the sample omission and warn that automatic capture can report available without supporting multiple captures (old raw lines 33-35, 344-346, 776-778). Map Advanced to direct PaymentIntents rather than implying it is a Checkout Sessions Elements integration (wiki/concepts/stripe-multicapture.md:19-23).

May embedded return-page prose labels `complete` as payment success (old raw lines 530-561). The November Checkout Session API object separately defines Session `status` and `payment_status` and explicitly allows processing after `complete` (raw/stripe-api-checkout-sessions-object-2026-11-07.md:306-325,362-380). Keep the embedded return UI separate from server-side PaymentIntent capture outcome, including when routing through the related Checkout concept.

Current source line 17 and wiki/concepts/stripe-multicapture.md:10 phrase pricing as absolute IC+ only/required. Old raw lines 14-16, 325-327 and 758-760 say Stripe offers the feature to IC+ users and directs blended pricing users seeking access to contact support. Preserve that route without implying Stripe grants access.

findings: New raw lines 5-15 are navigation beyond the same definition in old raw lines 4-6. Retain source lines 6-7 and 76-78 as historical behavioral provenance and add a navigation reference dated November.

answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/multicapture says one PaymentIntent can be captured multiple times up to its authorized amount and lists Stripe-hosted, full embedded and Advanced web routes (new raw lines 5-15). The May 11 full guide explains the IC+ offering and blended-pricing support route, eligible online cards and geography, 50-capture limit, manual capture and the Connect source_transaction restriction (old raw lines 14-35). Hosted and embedded Checkout create a Session whose confirmation creates the PaymentIntent, while Advanced works directly on a PaymentIntent. The merchant requests multicapture with if_available and checks latest_charge status in the eligible manual flow. The server captures a requires_capture PaymentIntent. A non-final partial capture keeps the remaining authorization, and final capture or expiry releases uncaptured authorization. An uncaptured Intent cancels on expiry while a partially captured Intent succeeds on finalization (old raw lines 137-222, old raw lines 364-415, old raw lines 752-938). source-stripe-multicapture.md summarizes the May variants and operational rules. Its existing expiry and zero-capture shorthand at lines 31-35 needs the prior-capture and state distinction independently of the November index.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/multicapture, new raw lines 5-15 preserve the definition and replace detailed variant bodies in the canonical capture with navigation. They do not establish a substantive product change. source-stripe-multicapture.md should retain May 11 conditions for request options, 50 captures, card and geography eligibility, Connect, refunds, webhooks and the manual capture and authorization state boundaries (old raw lines 14-35, old raw lines 137-317, old raw lines 794-1033). The embedded sample omits the documented manual parameter, and in May an automatic or automatic_async request could return available while the Intent was automatically captured in full (old raw lines 329-346, old raw lines 364-415). Warn reciprocally in Stripe Multicapture about both hazards and the distinction between an uncaptured expiry/cancellation, a partially captured Intent becoming succeeded, and the zero-amount release after prior partial capture. The embedded Session complete label in old raw lines 530-561 represents a Checkout flow state and its return does not establish PaymentIntent capture or settlement. Keep the May migration guide's beta-to-GA header, full-remaining non-final capture error and webhook changes dated to that separate migration context. Neither the November paths nor historical examples establish current merchant access or network compliance.
